messages:
Alex: Quick proposal — rather than spinning per-customer VPC peering for low-throughput customers, add a lightweight CP egress shim that multiplexes control-plane traffic and preserves source IP when needed. Sketch attached below.

Priya: +1 to avoiding peering explosion. What's the failure mode if the shim saturates?

Alex: Good q. We plan soft limits per-tenant + backpressure -> graceful fallback to dedicated peering. In practice the shim handles control-plane only, not data path.

Dan: How do we preserve audit/logging and per-tenant IP attestations? Need to keep source identity intact for RBAC and audits.

Alex: Two options: 1) proxy-preserve: shim rewrites X-Forwarded-For with tenant cert thumbprint and logs the original src IP, or 2) tunnel-handoff: short-lived ephemeral SNAT mapping that maps back on the receiving side. Both add complexity.

Marta: Option 1 seems simpler operationally but might break downstream security teams expecting raw src IP. Option 2 needs mapping table scaling. What's expected QPS for CP calls?

Alex: Observed CP QPS per small tenant is ~0.2 req/s avg, bursts to 5 req/s. So multiplexing gives lots of headroom.

Sally: Any latency SLO impact? We promised <100ms P99 for control-plane ops in Dedicated customers.

Alex: Shim adds ~8-15ms median with batching off; with microbatching it's ~20-30ms. Still under SLO, but can hurt cold path for tiny RPCs. We can expose a per-tenant mode: low-latency bypass (direct peering) vs cost-mode (multiplex).

Priya: We should enumerate rollout plan. My suggestion: Beta with internal-only tenants -> monitor CPU, connection counts, tail latency, and mapping table size. Then opt-in for small customers.

Dan: Also need threat model: does shim increase blast radius if compromised? We need mTLS end-to-end and token attestation.

Alex: Agreed — mTLS client certs + signed ephemeral tokens. Shim never has plaintext tokens; it passes opaque attestation to CP services.

InfraBot: Note: creating a global mapping table will require >50k entries for projected growth in 12 months. Consider sharding by region. :robot_face:

Marta: Sharding by region + LRU eviction for inactive tenants sounds reasonable. We'll need metrics: mapping_hits, mapping_evictions, shim_queue_depth, shim_cpu.

Sally: Ops playbook: alert on mapping_evictions rate > 1/min and queue_depth > 100 for >5m. Also add fallback to dedicated peering for flagged tenants.

Alex: Prototype config snippet: 
```
shims:
  egress_shim: true
  mode: multiplex
  per_tenant_limits: {"connections": 50, "qps": 100}
  auth: {"mtls": true, "attest_mode": "signed-token"}
```

Priya: Nice. One more: add a header for "x-redwood-tenant-id" and sign it. Downstream can verify without trusting shim.

Alex: Will add signed header.

Dan: Ok, can someone file an RFC follow-up with a diagram and concrete rollout milestones? I can help with the security section.

Alex: I'll draft RFC follow-up today, include benchmarks and failure scenarios. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
